Analysis: MCP works with session IDs via SSE. I'll write a small Python client to call MCP tools more conveniently.
Plan: Create a Python helper to initialize an MCP session and call tools, then list confluence tools.
bash_command

cat > /tmp/mcp_call.py << 'PY'
import json, sys, urllib.request

def call(base, method, params=None, session=None, mid=1):
    url = base if base.endswith('/') else base + '/'
    body = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": mid, "method": method}
    if params is not None:
        body["params"] = params
    data = json.dumps(body).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method='POST')
    req.add_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
    req.add_header('Accept', 'application/json, text/event-stream')
    if session:
        req.add_header('Mcp-Session-Id', session)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as resp:
        sid = resp.headers.get('mcp-session-id') or session
        raw = resp.read().decode()
    # parse SSE
    msgs = []
    for line in raw.splitlines():
        if line.startswith('data: '):
            msgs.append(json.loads(line[6:]))
    return sid

import asyncio
import re
from explore_parsed import call_json

def clean_html(raw):
    text = re.sub(r'</(p|div|h[1-6]|li|tr|ul|ol|table)>', '\n', raw)
    text = re.sub(r'<(br|hr)\s*/?>', '\n', text)
    text = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', text)
    import html
    text = html.unescape(text)
    return re.sub(r'\n\s*\n+', '\n', text).strip()

async def main():
    cursor = None
    all_pages = []
    while True:
        args = {"limit": 100, "body-format": "storage"}
        if cursor:
            args["cursor"] = cursor
        pages = await call_json("confluence-gym", "get_pages", args)
        for p in pages.get("results", []):
            all_pages.append(p)
        links = pages.get("_links", {})
        next_link = links.get("next")
        if next_link and "cursor=" in next_link:
            cursor = next_link.split("cursor=")[1].split("&")[0]
